text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- The WNordic Skiing World Championships open in Trondheim today.

- Aage Korsvold, head of Norway's largest insurance company Storebrand ASA, says he will focus on future growth of the group. Korsvold will keep Storebrand as an independent company based in Norway, but says the company is open to alliances and cooperation across borders.

- Saga Petroleum said on Wednesday that higher oil prices and production, as well as reduced costs, accounted for a 78 percent surge in 1996 operating profits to a record 3.32 billion crowns (492 million).
- Svein Eggen, head of offshore group Aker Maritime ASA, says the company will double turnover by 2000 to about 20 billion crowns.

- Oekokrim, the police unit for financial crime, may investigate software house Sysdeco ASA because of a recent report from the Oslo bourse authorities. Management at the bourse says that last years Sysdeco presented preliminary results for 1995 which gave false and misleading information about the company's financial situation.
